As blood leaves the heart Baroreceptors (aortic arch, carotid arteries)  Medulla vasomotor center  If BP High  Parasympathetic stimulation If BP Low  Sympathetic stimulation As blood travels through kidneys Low BP or poor oxygen (nephron)  Juxtaglomerular cells release RENIN  Renin reacts with ANGIOTENSINOGEN (made in liver)  This produces ANGIOTENSIN I  In lungs, angiotensin I converted to ANGIOTENSIN II via ANGIOTENSIN CONVERTING ENZYME (ACE)  Angiotensin II stimulates vasoconstriction, raising PVR & BP, and ALDOSTERONE release from adrenal cortex  Aldosterone stimulates nephrons to retain Na++ and H2O

title: Contraindications/Cautions: mannitol Condition Why Mannitol is Dangerous Severe renal disease / anuria (no uri
text: Contraindications/Cautions: mannitol Condition Why Mannitol is Dangerous Severe renal disease / anuria (no urine output) If the kidneys can’t make urine, mannitol can’t be excreted . It just stays in the bloodstream, pulling in more water into blood vessels — leading to fluid overload and worsening kidney damage . Pulmonary congestion or edema Mannitol pulls fluid from tissues into the bloodstream. If the heart or lungs are already overloaded, this extra volume can worsen pulmonary edema (fluid in the lungs) and cause shortness of breath or hypoxia . Dehydration Mannitol causes further water loss through diuresis, which can make dehydration much worse and cause electrolyte imbalances or hypotension. Heart failure (HF) In HF, the heart can’t pump effectively. Mannitol increases blood volume (as it pulls water from tissues), which can overwhelm the heart , leading to fluid buildup in the lungs and worsening heart failure.
